unit.why: A single anecdote about R. Jonathan Eybeschütz (author of Kreti u-Feleti) visiting the Pnei Yehoshua and perceiving his daughter's ritual impurity. Both are pre-Hasidic rabbinic figures, so the anecdote is not Hasidic.
unit.boundary_note: The trailing heading 'מענין טרדות' belongs to the next section.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי מהורי ואבותי אשר בעת נבחר
stories.summary_en: During the amulet controversy, the Pnei Yehoshua hosts the author of Kreti u-Feleti, who tells him that the daughter serving preserves has found a stain and cannot purify herself today; the Pnei Yehoshua checks and finds this true.

tags.why: The story praises the supernatural insight of R. Jonathan Eybeschütz, a pre-Hasidic sage, and is taken from an earlier book's introduction.

quotes: תדעו כי היום מצאה כתם ולא תוכל להטהר
tags.why: He knows of the hidden stain without being told.

quotes: מצאה כתם ולא תוכל להטהר היום
tags.why: The point turns on the laws of menstrual purity, a stain blocking immersion.
The host sage's daughter appears in the story.
The daughter acts by serving preserves but is peripheral.

quotes: בעניני הקמיעות אשר היה על הג׳ בעל כרתי ופלתי
tags.why: The amulet controversy forms the backdrop only.

quotes: בעת נבחר לשבת לדין בעניני הקמיעות
tags.why: The Emden–Eybeschütz amulet controversy sets the scene.

quotes: ולא תוכל להטהר היום אף כי הוא זמנה
tags.why: Purification is not allowed that day.
